about: Formats modelled on clean Shorts that outperformed their channel's usual views (vidIQ outliers, Jul-Oct 2026). We copy structure and pacing only, never footage or scripts. Every Short picks one format; the writer fills the beats in order.

global_rules.hook: First spoken line states the stakes or the mystery in under 2.5 s and names the subject. No 'did you know', no greetings, no view counts or 'this went viral'.
global_rules.pace: Narration 2.4-2.8 words a second, with a real pause before the reveal and after any rhetorical question.
global_rules.re_hook: Around 45-60% of the runtime, one short pivot line ('But here's the strange part.', 'So why now?') to reset attention.
global_rules.visuals: New shot every 1.5-3 s. The first time a person appears, show their name label. Zoom or flash on the reveal word, with an impact sound. Real footage of the subject beats stock.
global_rules.ending: End on a payoff line that reframes the opening, or an open question that invites comments. 'Follow for more' only after the payoff, never instead of it.
global_rules.length: Single-reveal 20-35 s, lists 25-40 s, explainers 30-45 s, timelines up to 60 s. Cut anything that doesn't move the story.

formats.name: One detail explains it
formats.use_when: A trailer, reveal, photo or clip contains one telling detail that changes how you read it.

beats.say: In [thing], [who] hides one detail that explains everything.
beats.visual: title card over the best shot of the subject

beats.say: [The detail].
beats.visual: tight zoom or flash cut onto the detail, impact sound

beats.say: Why it matters: what we already knew (1-2 beats).
beats.visual: the person or place, with name label

beats.say: But here's what makes it bigger.
Supporting facts, each with its own shot (2-3 beats, can be a quick list).
One line that reframes the opening.
Date or what happens next. Follow for more.

examples.title: The Trailer Had One Hidden Trick
This weird detail in the Fortnite trailer
GTA 6's launch trailer hides its whole story in one detail (ours, QD-027)

formats.name: 3 details you missed
formats.use_when: A new trailer, episode, game update or product launch with several small, checkable details.

beats.say: Three details in [thing] almost nobody noticed.
One: [detail], and what it means.
beats.visual: zoom on the detail, big number 1

beats.say: Two: [detail], and what it means.
But the third one is the best.
Three: the strongest detail, saved for last.
Open question about which one matters most.

examples.title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs Hidden Details You Missed!
3 Hidden RDR2 Details You Definitely Missed

formats.name: Big news, explained
formats.use_when: A launch, leak, signing, record or announcement that people are searching for today.

beats.say: [Who] might be about to [big move], and [rival or surprising cause] could be the reason.
beats.visual: close, tactile shot of the subject

beats.say: What's new, fast: 2-4 facts, one per shot.
beats.visual: cards or labels for numbers and dates

beats.say: So why now?
The real reason, with the evidence.
beats.visual: the rival, the document or the moment

beats.say: And here's the part that matters most: [consequence].
Open question that invites a debate in the comments.

examples.title: Galaxy Z Tri-Fold 2 - All the Big Changes Explained!
examples.notes: 13 shots, average 2.8 s; about 2.4 words a second; rivalry hook (Samsung vs Apple); 'But why the sudden rush?' reset at 0:11; 'And here's the exciting part' at 0:20; ends on an open question.

formats.name: Everything in 60 seconds
formats.use_when: A franchise, rivalry or person with a clear history that a new event makes relevant again.

beats.say: Every [X], explained in 60 seconds.
One beat per era or entry, oldest first, year on screen.
beats.visual: date card or label per beat, 1.5-2.5 s cuts

beats.say: Then everything changed.
Today's news and why it breaks the pattern.
What comes next, with a date if known.

examples.title: Every C8 Corvette Explained in 90 Seconds

formats.name: The real reason
formats.use_when: Something surprising happened (a delay, a missing platform, a record, a rule) and the cause isn't obvious.

beats.say: [Surprising fact]. The reason isn't what you think.
What most people assume.
But look at [evidence].
The actual reason, in two beats, with sources on screen.
What it means for the next thing people are waiting for.
